entries.title: Bears report: Offensive line uncertainty as Jonah Jackson injured, decision to make at left tackle
entries.summary: <p>What happened Monday at Halas Hall:</p><h3><b>Jackson in jeopardy</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> didn’t practice Monday, but were required to release an estimated injury report and didn’t think right guard Jonah Jackson (hip) would’ve been available. Jackson went down in the second half of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-cb-kyler-gordon-goes-off-with-3-sacks-in-return-from-injury-everything-i-wanted" >the win over the Falcons</a>, and Luke Newman replaced him. Jackson hasn’t missed a start in two seasons with the Bears.</p><p></p><h3><b>Monangai still sidelined</b></h3><h3></h3><p>No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai, an integral part of the ground game alongside D’Andre Swift, looks unlikely to be back against the Patriots. Monangai has missed two games with a toe injury, and the Bears said he wouldn’t have practiced Monday. If he’s out, Roschon Johnson is likely to continue getting a decent share of carries.</p><p></p><h3><b>Doubs out</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Patriots put wide receiver Romeo Doubs, formerly of the Packers, on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. He leads them with 261 yards and three touchdowns.</p><p></p><h3><b>Bagent stays backup</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Tyson Bagent’s spot as the backup quarterback was in question after he got benched against the Packers, but coach Ben Johnson kept him in the No. 2 spot Sunday and made third-stringer Case Keenum the inactive emergency quarterback.</p><p></p><h3><b>Left tackle decision</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears eventually want Ozzy Trapilo to step back into his spot as the starting left tackle, and playing a few series Sunday in his season debut was a step toward that. Ben Johnson must weigh whether he’s ready for more or to stay predominantly with Theo Benedet.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser
